title: sw-dev-blueprint frozen contracts (scripts/.approved/contracts.json)
description: The machine-readable section of the TPM's ERD: the locked cross-component surface. The TPM authors it in the web chat; the human installs it via scripts/refreeze.sh; no agent can write it (it lives outside every lane and is hash-pinned in scripts/.approved/frozen-manifest). Everything listed here is LOCKED — the EM owns implementation inside these seams and may not invent or alter them. INV-4 additionally requires that the frozen tests observe the system ONLY through surfaces declared here (test-visible surface must be a subset of the locked surface).

erd_version.description: Must equal scripts/.approved/VERSION. Bumped only by refreeze.sh.

files.description: The ERD build inventory: every source file the feature requires, relative to repo root. The plan gate requires exactly one task per listed file — coverage failures surface at validation, not integration.

entry_points.description: Importable symbols tests may use, as 'module' or 'module:symbol' (e.g. 'src.main' or 'src.main:app'). INV-4: any import of src.* in tests/ outside this list fails the surface gate.

id.description: Stable contract id, e.g. 'route:GET /health'. Referenced by plan tasks.

file.description: D-120: the source file that owns this entry — the file whose code must satisfy it. Enables the mechanical contracts-delta slice for the EM's per-milestone context. entry_points need no tag (dotted paths derive their file).

routes.description: HTTP surface. INV-4: any route-shaped string a test sends a request to must appear here.

fields.description: Field name -> type, as locked by the TPM.

file.description: D-120: the source file that owns this entry.

schemas.description: Data shapes crossing a seam (request/response bodies, persisted records).

file.description: D-120: the source file that owns this entry.

probe.description: The exact shell command the operator ran against the REAL dependency to produce the capture (e.g. a curl). Re-runnable to detect upstream drift.

capture.description: Path under captures/ (staged next to the spec, installed to scripts/.approved/captures/) holding the probe's raw output. This is the ground truth mocks are built from.

notes.description: Optional: what the spec relies on from this capture (fields, event names, formats).

externals.description: D-56: every external interface the spec makes assumptions about (third-party APIs, model output formats, wire protocols) must be declared here with a captured real response. refreeze.sh fails the freeze if a declared capture is missing. Mocks and tests derive from captures, never from the TPM's memory of how the dependency probably behaves.

test_mapping.description: M35 correction: the TPM's frozen declaration of behavioral ownership — maps each delta node-id to the inventory file that behaviorally owns it (one entry per node-id; the file must be in the files array). The plan gate places every pinned node-id at the task owning its pinned file, wherever the EM mapped it; placement is derived from this data, never from a heuristic or an EM interpretation. check-spec-delta.py rejects keys that are not frozen node-ids and targets outside the files array.

smoke_checks.description: TPM-authored shell commands keyed by file path (from the files array). Used for files with no covering frozen test — the orchestrator runs them in the sandbox after the coder writes the file. An oracle: authored by the TPM (frontier), installed via refreeze.sh, never by the EM. Each value must be a valid shell command, not prose.

testid.description: The data-testid value the implementation must carry and UI tests locate by. The ONLY DOM surface frozen tests may observe (D-58) — check-test-surface.py rejects role/text/CSS/XPath location in playwright-importing tests.

description.description: What the element is, so the coder knows where the testid belongs.

file.description: D-120: the source file that owns this entry — the file whose code must satisfy it. UI files live under src/static (JS/HTML); the pattern intentionally differs from the Python .py pins on routes/schemas/errors.

ui.description: D-58: the locked DOM surface. Same principle as routes/entry_points — tests observe only what the spec locks, so the coder is free to restructure everything else. Testids reach the coder via contracts in the brief material.

changed_files.description: D-86: the inventory files THIS delta's work touches, declared by the TPM. refreeze.sh copies it verbatim into DELTA-vN.json's changed_files, which --affected unions with the test/contract deltas to derive the coder's editable set. Before D-86 this field did not exist and refreeze hardcoded changed_files to [], so scope was reachable only through the EM's test mapping — a containment boundary set implicitly by the mid tier (testchat M31: index.html was uneditable for a milestone that needed markup in it). Declare a file here to put it in scope deliberately. Every entry must also appear in files; it is a per-delta declaration, so re-state it at every freeze — a stale entry silently widens the next delta's scope.

no_edit_files.description: D-65: inventory files this frozen spec declares unchanged ('NO EDIT NEEDED' in the ERD). The orchestrator does not invoke the coder for their tasks — briefing a local model to 'change nothing' is a negative constraint it cannot reliably obey (testchat M16: a no-edit coder call damaged index.html, a second added redundant code). Acceptance (mapped tests + smoke_check) still runs. Every entry must also appear in files.
